Brand guidelines · Stage 3 · 2026-11-21

Slonview Brand Guidelines

  • Stage: 3, full identity system for Concept A, "Viewport in motion". The owner chose it at Gate 2 with no further notes.
  • Date: 2026-11-21
  • Sources: the brand strategy (cited below as "strategy §N": §6 claims, §9 taglines, §10–11 visual brief), the Stage 2 concept review, and slonview-verbal-identity.md. The strategy, concept review and QA reports are internal working documents and are not published. The claim rules they set are restated where they apply: here and in the claim cheat sheet in slonview-verbal-identity.md.
  • Assets: docs/brand/identity/. Every file is generated by docs/brand/identity/build/build.py (Python, fontTools, HarfBuzz, skia-pathops, Pillow, rsvg-convert). Change the build script, then re-run it; don't hand-edit the outputs.

1. The idea

The mark is a closed window frame with one highlighted row passing through a notch in its right wall. Two quiet rows stay inside the frame.

  • Small app, whole table (internal design rationale, not public copy). The frame is small and the row is longer than the frame. This is the brand's speed and size lead in one shape. Public copy may say "whole table" only about export until the WKWebView scrolling check passes (strategy §12).
  • It is the paging mechanism. Slonview pages through a fixed window, 500 rows at a time. The row shown in transit is the page moving through the view.
  • Motion comes from offset and crop. There are no speed lines, swooshes or blur.
  • Red stays free. The accent is plum on light grounds and lilac on dark grounds. Red is used only for the WRITE badge and for errors.
2 s loop · static under reduced motion

3. Logo system

3.1 Files

AssetColourwaysFormats
Symbol (64-unit master)light, dark, mono, reversedidentity/symbol/symbol-<mode>.svg, @1x.png (128 px), @2x.png (256 px)
Symbol, hand-tuned 32 pxlight, dark, mono, reversedsymbol-32px-<mode>.svg, .png (32), @2x.png (64)
Symbol, hand-tuned 16 pxlight, dark, mono, reversedsymbol-16px-<mode>.svg, .png (16), @2x.png (32)
Wordmark (outlined)light, dark, mono, reversedidentity/wordmark/wordmark-<mode>.svg, @1x.png, @2x.png
Wordmark (editable text)lightidentity/wordmark/wordmark-editable.svg (layout drafts only; needs ../fonts/)
Horizontal lockuplight, dark, mono, reversedidentity/lockup/lockup-horizontal-<mode>.svg, @1x.png (560×128), @2x.png
Motion studylightidentity/motion/symbol-motion-light.svg

Each colourway has a ground it is meant for:

  • light: Paper #F4F5F8 or white;
  • dark: Graphite #1B1D21 or #212328;
  • mono: any light ground, in one colour (ink);
  • reversed: plum #6E2366, ink, or a photograph darker than L* 35, in white.

Every outlined SVG is free of <text>, <image>, data:image, font-family and filters. The build script checks this on every run.

3.2 Construction

  • Symbol (64 grid):
    • Frame: 44 × 40 at (4, 12), corner radius 9, wall 5.5.
    • Row: 8 tall at y 28, running from x 13 to x 61, with fully rounded ends.
    • Notch: row height + 1.6 above and below.
    • Quiet rows: 24 × 3.6 at y 20.6 and y 39.8.
  • Wordmark:
    • Hanken Grotesk at wght 640 with −0.012 em tracking, outlined.
    • The dot of the "i" is replaced by a short plum row: 2.1 × stem width, 0.92 × stem height, starting at the stem's left edge.
    • This keeps "Slonview" one unbroken word. There is no gap after "Slo" (strategy §8.2).
  • Lockup:
    • Symbol height = 1.55 × the wordmark's cap height.
    • Gap between symbol and wordmark = 0.42 × symbol height.
    • The two are optically centred on the cap height.

3.3 Clearspace

The unit R is the height of the accent row in the symbol (8/64 of the symbol height).

  • Keep at least 3R clear on all sides of the symbol and of the lockup. Measure from the frame on the left, top and bottom, and from the row's tip on the right.
  • On the wordmark alone, keep 1R at the wordmark's own scale (the height of the i-dot row × 1.1) on all sides.
  • The row's right tip is part of the mark. Never crop it, and never let another element touch it.

3.4 Minimum sizes

AssetScreen minimumPrint minimumBelow the minimum
Symbol, 64 master24 px tall8 mmUse the 32 px master from 24 to 39 px, and the 16 px master below 24 px
Symbol, 16 px master16 px—Don't go smaller
Horizontal lockup24 px tall (wordmark cap ≈ 13 px)25 mm wideUse the symbol alone
Wordmark alone72 px wide18 mm wideUse the symbol alone
App icon16 px (hand-tuned master)——

At 16 px, use the colour icon or the colour symbol. The mono 16 px master is the weakest form (it comes closest to a "list in a box"), so use it only where a single colour is forced, such as a one-colour favicon set or a print stamp.

3.5 Misuse

The sheet above (identity/checks/misuse.png) shows eight real misuses of the mark:

  1. Red row. Red belongs to WRITE and errors.
  2. Old UI blue (or any other new accent).
  3. Squashing or stretching.
  4. Rotating.
  5. Opening the right wall. This brings back the logout reading MAJOR-2 removed.
  6. Adding speed lines, motion blur or swooshes.
  7. Baking in a drop shadow or glow. Platforms add their own.
  8. Placing it on a ground below 3:1 for any part. Light colourway on graphite is one example.

Also don't:

  • put the mark next to, or inside, a PostgreSQL or Slonik mark (strategy §6.4);
  • set "Slonview" in another font in place of the outlined wordmark;
  • recolour the quiet rows to the accent (they would then read as a hamburger);
  • animate the mark inside the app (the app has no splash screen).

4. App icon

4.1 Files

docs/brand/identity/appicon/:

  • icon-light-1024.svg and icon-dark-1024.svg: the layered masters. <g id="background"> holds a flat gradient tile on the macOS grid (824 px tile on a 1024 canvas, radius 185.4) with no shadow. <g id="foreground"> holds the symbol at 74 % of the tile.
  • PNG at 1024, 512, 256, 128, 64, 32 and 16 px, for both light and dark. The 32 and 16 px PNGs are rendered from the hand-tuned icon-<appearance>-32.svg and -16.svg masters, not downscaled.
  • layer-background-light.svg, layer-background-dark.svg: background only.
  • layer-foreground-colour.svg, layer-foreground-white.svg, layer-foreground-tint-greyscale.svg: foreground only, transparent ground.
  • icon.svg: a copy of the light master. This is the layered source that src-tauri/icons/icon.svg uses.

4.2 Appearances

AppearanceTileFrameQuiet rowsRow
Light (default)#7A2A71 → #5A1C54#F4F5F8#B8BEC8#D9A8FA
Dark#30333A → #1B1D21, white 14 % inner rim#DFE2E7#868D98#D9A8FA

macOS tinted and clear appearances (macOS 26 Icon Composer). Not delivered as a .icon bundle, because Icon Composer is a GUI app. To build one:

  1. Import layer-background-light.svg as the background group and layer-foreground-tint-greyscale.svg as the foreground group. The foreground is white frame, #E6E6E6 row and #B3B3B3 quiet rows, so macOS's tint keeps the row-versus-frame hierarchy.
  2. For Clear, use layer-foreground-white.svg with the system's default glass. The notch and the row's overhang still read, because they are shape, not colour.
  3. Don't add specular highlights or shadows. Icon Composer adds them.

4.3 Install in the app

Installed in src-tauri/icons/ by docs/brand/identity/build/install_icons.sh:

  1. pnpm tauri icon docs/brand/identity/appicon/icon-light-1024.png generates the desktop set. The android/ and ios/ outputs are deleted, because Slonview is desktop only.
  2. tauri icon only downscales, so the script then rebuilds icon.icns with iconutil and icon.ico with Pillow (16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 256), using the hand-tuned 16 and 32 px masters. It also replaces 32x32.png.

Verified by extracting the installed icon.icns: its icon_16x16.png is pixel-identical to the hand-tuned icon-light-16.png. tauri.conf.json is unchanged; it already points at 32x32.png, 128x128.png, 128x128@2x.png, icon.icns and icon.ico.

4.4 Small-size and distinctiveness checks

Checks rendered:

  • identity/checks/misread-16px.png: every comparison glyph at 8× and 1:1, on Finder light #ECECEE and dark #1E1E20.
  • identity/checks/appicon-sizes.png: every size, both appearances, on both backdrops.
  • identity/checks/appicon-16-tuned-vs-downscaled.png.
  • Headless-browser renders: render-dock.png (Dock in light and dark), render-finder.png (Finder list at 16 px, Spotlight at 32 px), render-symbols.png, render-small.png, render-applications.png.

What the 16 px icon reads as now:

  • A closed square frame with three bars. The middle bar is lilac and runs through the frame's right wall.
  • Logout and exit: these glyphs are an open bracket with an arrowhead. Slonview has no arrowhead, its frame is closed on all four sides apart from the notch, and its row is a bar with two bars beside it.
  • C, G, €: the right wall above and below the row is now 3 px tall at 16 px, so the frame no longer reads as an open curve.
  • Battery: the battery's nub is short, centred and outside a hollow box. Slonview's row starts inside the frame and extends 3 px out, and two quiet rows sit inside.
  • Hamburger: the quiet rows are shorter and lighter than the row, and the frame is closed.
  • Scrollbar and progress bar: the bar is horizontal and crosses the wall, which neither control does.

Silhouette overlap (mono 16 px, intersection over union of ink pixels, best of ±2 px shifts; lower is more distinct):

The progress-bar overlap rose slightly, because the closed frame is now a longer horizontal box. In colour it does not read as a progress bar: the frame is ink or fog, not a track, and two quiet rows sit inside it. The IoU is a shape heuristic. Visual inspection of the sheet is the deciding check.

Competitors: the side-by-side comparison with other PostgreSQL clients' icons (TablePlus, Postico, DBeaver, Beekeeper, Tabularis, PostgresGUI, Slonik) at 256, 32 and 16 px was done during internal review and is not published, because it reproduces third-party icons. At every size the Slonview icon was the only plum tile in that set, and none of those icons uses a frame-and-row shape.

Method:

  • CIELAB with a D65 white, ΔE76.
  • Colour-vision deficiency simulated with the Machado 2009 matrices at severity 1.0, applied in linear sRGB.
  • Code: identity/build/colour.py.

Watch items:

  • Lilac is 37° from indigo by hue. Don't drift it bluer than 272°.
  • Lilac is a mid-chroma pastel. Keep it on graphite grounds, never as a large background fill, so the brand doesn't read as Harlequin's pastel set.

7. Typography

RoleTypefaceWeightsSizes (app)FeaturesFallback stack
WordmarkHanken Grotesk, outlined640——none (outlined)
UI textHanken Grotesk400 body, 500 labels, 600 headings and badges13 px body (current base), 11 px meta, 10 px badges (600, +0.04 em, all caps), 15 px dialog titlesFigures are uniform width by default: all ten digits measure 560 units, verified in the font.-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, system-ui, "Segoe UI", sans-serif
Headlines (web, README, social)Hanken Grotesk650–680, −0.01 to −0.02 em40 px README, 60 px social card—as above
SQL, grid data, figuresJetBrains Mono400 data, 600 headers and PK marker12 px grid cells, 12 px editor, 11 px type namesMonospaced, so tabular by construction; zero for slashed zero in IDs; calt off in the SQL editorui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, monospace

Rules:

  • One display face, used with restraint. Hanken carries both the UI and the headlines; only weight and size separate them.
  • Numbers are the brand's proof. Set measured figures in JetBrains Mono beside a Hanken headline (README header, social card).
  • Use sentence case everywhere, except the badges READ-ONLY and WRITE, which are verbatim UI strings.
  • App implementation note: the app bundles Hanken Grotesk and JetBrains Mono as WOFF2 (about 130 KB together, OFL) in the frontend. The fallback stack is the safety net.

Footer: "Local benchmark: 1,000,000-row orders table · PostgreSQL® 18.4 over Unix socket · MacBook Air (Mac17,3, Apple M5)". This meets §6.2 rule 2: dataset, version, connection, machine. The machine is confirmed: QA read sysctl -n hw.model → Mac17,3 (MacBook Air, Apple M5) and PostgreSQL 18.4 on the local socket /tmp/.s.PGSQL.5432.
README header, 1280 × 320, light and darkidentity/readme/readme-header-{light,dark}.svg / .png / @2x.png"Ready for a million rows." with the number directly under it: "1,000,000-row CSV export in ~0.44 s / local benchmark: PostgreSQL 18.4, Unix socket, MacBook Air (Mac17,3, Apple M5)", then line #3. Use a <picture> with prefers-color-scheme sources.

All text in these images is outlined (no <text>). Their <title> holds the words for screen readers. When placing them in the README, give the <img> an alt that repeats the headline and the benchmark label.

9. Motion

  • File: identity/motion/symbol-motion-light.svg.
  • Loop: 2 s. The row slides 48 units from the left, inside the frame, eases out at 70 % of the loop (cubic-bezier .2, .7, .2, 1), and holds in its static position.
  • Clip: a rectangle the height of the notch keeps the row inside the frame until it exits.
  • Reduced motion: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .sv-row { animation: none } }. The static mark is the resting frame. Verified in headless Chromium: the animation name is sv-slide by default and none with reduced motion emulated.
  • Where: the website, the launch video and social media only. Never in the app, and never as a splash screen.

10. Font and licence inventory

identity/fonts/ holds HankenGrotesk[wght].ttf, JetBrainsMono[wght].ttf, the full OFL 1.1 texts (OFL-hankengrotesk.txt, OFL-jetbrainsmono.txt), the Lucide ISC licence (LICENSE-lucide.txt, including the MIT notice for icons derived from Feather), and LICENSES.md (copyright lines, sources and usage).

11. Brand-to-UI token map

  • Files: identity/tokens.json (values, roles, the colours each token replaces, and the three usage rules) and identity/tokens.css (--sv-* custom properties: light by default, dark under prefers-color-scheme: dark, matching the app's current switch).
  • Wiring: point the app's existing @theme names (--color-accent, …) at these variables, replace the ResultGrid.tsx PALETTES values and draw-callback literals with the matching tokens, and replace oneDark with an EditorView.theme built from §11.2. Not applied in this stage.
  • Usage rules:
    1. On a selection, secondary text (faint, null-fg, warn / PK) switches to selection-fg-muted.
    2. On accent fills, text uses accent-fg; secondary text uses accent-fg-muted.
    3. On accent-soft (the selected sidebar or connection row), faint text such as the row count (Sidebar.tsx:182) switches to muted: 5.53 light, 5.73 dark. faint there is 4.07 / 4.42.
    4. On error fills, text uses error-fg.
    5. Never lower text contrast with opacity or alpha (opacity-*, text-*/NN, inline opacity). Use muted, faint or accent-fg-muted instead. The context-menu shortcut (ContextMenu.tsx:83, opacity-60) becomes muted on an unhighlighted item (7.40 / 6.55) and accent-fg-muted on the highlighted item (6.34 / 5.35; 60 % ink on lilac is 3.64). The only exemptions are disabled controls and 0/100 show-hide toggles, which carry no readable text contrast.

12. Remaining risks

  1. No FigCraft master (review MINOR-7, QA MINOR-A). GUI apps were out of scope for this run. The layered SVGs are the editable source; the owner should accept this at Gate 3 or schedule a FigCraft import.
  2. No macOS 26 .icon bundle. Tinted and clear appearances are specified (§4.2) and the layers are supplied, but nothing was rendered in Icon Composer.
  3. Size claim removed. The signed v0.1.0 build installs at 9.9 MB, so the owner dropped "about 8 MB" everywhere on 2026-11-22. Don't reintroduce a size number.
  4. Lilac is 37° from indigo by hue. It is distinct today (ΔE 45). Hold the hue at 272° or more.
  5. Editor numbers and error red under deuteranopia. Amber #E0B45C vs error dark is ΔE 50.1, but only 29.9 under deuteranopia. The error mark is a wavy underline plus a tinted background, never a text colour, so the two don't compete for the same role.
  6. Tokens are not wired into the app yet. src/index.css, ResultGrid.tsx and SqlEditor.tsx still use the old colours until the UI/UX stage applies tokens.css and §11.2.

13. How this document is built

docs/brand/identity/build/guidelines_html.py renders this Markdown to slonview-brand-guidelines.html. The HTML is one self-contained file: Hanken Grotesk and JetBrains Mono are embedded as base64 @font-face (OFL allows embedding), and every figure is an inline data URI. Headings get slug-only ids. The page uses the brand palette: paper #F4F5F8, ink #16181D, plum #6E2366.

Verified in headless Chromium: zero network requests, both embedded fonts report loaded, every image decodes, and no element overflows the page at 1280 px or 390 px. Wide tables scroll inside their own containers.

The full render-check gallery, which shows every exported asset, is docs/brand/identity/checks/gallery.html. It opens offline and loads files relative to itself.
